meta.subject: English Comprehension
meta.batch: sample-003 (post-review fixes: replaced 5 items resting on disputed / prescriptive-only rules — 'most unique', 'majority of ... was', 'every ... their', repeated emphatic 'himself', 'kind of' + article — with indisputable errors; softened 1 explanation ('a lot of useful information'); relabelled Q1 & Q8 to easy)
meta.canonical_format: 4-segment: sentence split into 4 parts by ' / '; exactly one part carries the error; options = the 4 parts. Target ~85% of every pool.
meta.variant_format: 3-part + 'No error' as option D. Deliberately ~15% of the pool; of those ~40% genuinely have no error so 'No error' is a real answer, not a never-right decoy. This batch: 5/30 (16.7%), 3 with answer = 'No error'.
meta.pyq_grounding: SSC CGL Tier-1 'Spot the Error' — 3-5 per paper. Real category weighting from released papers: subject-verb agreement, tense / verb-form / sequence of tenses, prepositions, articles & determiners, pronouns (case & reflexive), adjective-vs-adverb, degree of comparison, redundancy / superfluous words, parallelism, correlative conjunctions.
meta.difficulty_split: easy 11 / medium 14 / hard 5  (post-fix; hard still under target 25% — the next batch must add structurally-buried-error hard items, see brief §7)
meta.category_split: SVA 7 / tense-verbform 6 / preposition 5 / article-determiner 5 / pronoun 3 / adj-adv 2 / degree 2 / redundancy 1 / parallelism 1 / correlatives 1 / other 2 (incl. 5 'No error' items)
meta.reuse: Grammar + Vocabulary items are ~80% reusable for TNPSC General English and ~95% for SSC CHSL/MTS/CPO/GD and RRB English. NOT reusable for UPSC (CSAT English is reading comprehension only).

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The committee members / has decided / to postpone the annual meeting / until the first week of March.
options: until the first week of March.
questions.explanation: The subject 'members' is plural, so the verb must be plural: 'have decided', not 'has decided'. Trap: 'committee' looks singular, but the head noun controlling the verb here is 'members'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: subject-verb agreement)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Each of the students / were given / a separate hall ticket / for the online examination.
questions.explanation: 'Each of + plural noun' takes a singular verb, so 'were' should be 'was'. Trap: the plural 'students' just before the verb tempts you toward 'were'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: 'each of' + singular verb)

questions.question:
Select the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.
The train had already left / when we reached the platform / with our heavy luggage.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: past perfect ('had already left') for the earlier action, simple past ('reached') for the later one. 'No error'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error, 'No error' variant (rule: past perfect vs simple past)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The management / will implemented / the revised leave policy / from the beginning of next month.
options: from the beginning of next month.
questions.explanation: After the modal 'will', the verb must be in its base form: 'will implement', not 'will implemented'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: modal + base verb)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
He has been working / in this organisation / since eight years / without taking a single long leave.
options: without taking a single long leave.
questions.explanation: 'Since' marks a point in time; a stretch of time takes 'for'. It should be 'for eight years'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: since vs for)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Ravi is / the most honest colleague / I have ever worked with / in a office of this size.
options: in a office of this size.
questions.explanation: 'Office' begins with a vowel sound, so the article must be 'an', not 'a': 'in an office'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: a vs an)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Between you and I, / the newly appointed head / seems far more capable / than the previous one.
questions.explanation: After the preposition 'between', pronouns take the objective case: 'Between you and me'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: pronoun after preposition)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The visiting team played / very careless / in the second half / and threw away a comfortable lead.
options: and threw away a comfortable lead.
questions.explanation: An adverb, not an adjective, modifies the verb 'played': 'very carelessly'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: adjective vs adverb)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Most first-year students find algebra / more difficult / to geometry, / especially in the opening months.
questions.explanation: A comparative adjective ('more difficult') is followed by 'than', not 'to': 'more difficult than geometry'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: comparative + 'than')

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Kindly revert back / to us / at the earliest / so that we can confirm your booking.
options: so that we can confirm your booking.
questions.explanation: 'Revert' already means 'to come/reply back', so 'back' is redundant: 'Kindly revert'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: redundancy)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Neither the players / nor the coach / were satisfied / with the umpire's decision.
questions.explanation: With 'neither ... nor ...', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, here the singular 'coach': 'was satisfied'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: neither...nor, proximity agreement)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
A number of applications / was rejected / this year / because they arrived after the closing date.
options: because they arrived after the closing date.
questions.explanation: 'A number of + plural noun' is plural, so it takes 'were rejected'. Contrast: 'The number of ...' is singular.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: a number of vs the number of)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
One of the machines / in the packaging unit / have been malfunctioning / since early on Monday.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'One' (singular); 'of the machines' is only a modifier. The verb must be singular: 'has been malfunctioning'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: 'one of the + plural noun' takes a singular verb)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
My cousin was married / with a software engineer / who now works / at a firm in Pune.
questions.explanation: One is 'married to' someone, not 'married with': 'married to a software engineer'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: preposition with 'married')

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
He told the reporters / that he will meet / the striking workers / the following morning.
questions.explanation: In reported speech after a past reporting verb ('told'), 'will' backshifts to 'would': 'that he would meet'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: sequence of tenses in reported speech)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Honesty is / best policy / when you are dealing / with long-standing clients.
questions.explanation: The superlative needs the definite article: 'the best policy'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: 'the' with superlatives)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
My colleague and myself / were asked to represent / the department / at the regional conference.
questions.explanation: A reflexive pronoun ('myself') cannot be the subject of a verb. The subject form is 'I': 'My colleague and I were asked ...'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: reflexive pronoun cannot be a subject)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
She is one of those managers / who always insists / on double-checking every figure / before the report is released.
options: She is one of those managers
questions.explanation: In 'one of those + plural noun + who ...', the relative clause verb is plural because 'who' refers to 'managers': 'who always insist'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: 'one of those who' + plural verb)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The branch manager was angry / on his assistant / for failing to inform him / about the audit in advance.
questions.explanation: One is 'angry with' a person (and 'angry at/about' a thing): 'angry with his assistant'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: 'angry with' a person)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The consultant gave us / many useful informations / about the new tax regime / during the workshop.
questions.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable: no plural and no 'many'. It should be 'a lot of useful information' (or simply 'useful information').
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: uncountable nouns)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
It is nearly three years / since I have met / my former classmates / from the training academy.
questions.explanation: In the pattern 'It is + period + since ...', the 'since' clause takes the simple past: 'since I met'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: 'It is ... since' + simple past)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
On weekends she enjoys reading, sketching / and to cycle / along the river / with her neighbours.
options: On weekends she enjoys reading, sketching
questions.explanation: Parallelism: the list uses gerunds ('reading', 'sketching'), so the third item must match: 'and cycling'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: parallel structure)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The traffic situation near the market / became more worse / after the flyover / was closed for repairs.
options: The traffic situation near the market
questions.explanation: 'Worse' is already comparative; 'more worse' is a double comparative. It should be just 'worse'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: double comparatives)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
He is one of the finest player / the academy / has produced / in the last two decades.
options: He is one of the finest player
questions.explanation: 'One of the + superlative' is followed by a plural noun: 'one of the finest players'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: 'one of the' + plural noun)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Her assessment of the proposal / was quite different than / the view / put forward by the finance team.
options: put forward by the finance team.
questions.explanation: The standard idiom is 'different from': 'quite different from the view'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: 'different from')

questions.question:
Select the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.
Hardly had the minister finished his speech / when the crowd / rose to its feet and cheered.
options: Hardly had the minister finished his speech
rose to its feet and cheered.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: 'Hardly ... when ...' with inversion ('Hardly had ...') is the right structure. ('No sooner' pairs with 'than'; 'hardly/scarcely' pairs with 'when'.) 'No error'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error, 'No error' variant (rule: 'hardly ... when' correlative)

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
When we reached the auditorium, / the programme already started / and we had to / find seats in the dark.
questions.explanation: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect: 'the programme had already started'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: past perfect for the earlier action)

questions.question:
Select the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.
The principal congratulated the students / for their / brilliant results in the board examination.
options: brilliant results in the board examination.
questions.explanation: The idiom is 'congratulate someone ON something': 'congratulated the students on their brilliant results'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error, 'No error' variant (rule: 'congratulate on')

questions.question:
Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The university awarded her / a honorary doctorate / for her decades of research / on tropical diseases.
questions.explanation: 'Honorary' begins with a silent 'h', so it takes a vowel sound: 'an honorary doctorate', not 'a honorary doctorate'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error (rule: a/an by sound, silent 'h')

questions.question:
Select the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.
The conclusions of the new survey / are consistent with / those of the study conducted in 2019.
options: The conclusions of the new survey
those of the study conducted in 2019.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: 'consistent with' is the right preposition, and 'those of' correctly stands in for 'the conclusions of' in the comparison. 'No error'.
questions.source: SSC CGL Tier-1 English — Spot the Error, 'No error' variant (rule: 'consistent with' + parallel comparison with 'those of')
